claims.text: ADR 0012 (Accepted) weighs three options against CH-1 to CH-4: a copy of the whole system per shop, one shared deployment keeping the stage-3 shape, and splitting Ordering and Catalog further into services.
CH-1 to CH-4: each shop sees only its own data; a new shop opens without a deploy; one shop's busy day does not slow the others; each shop has its own settings.

Copy per shop (ADR lines 23-26): best isolation, a busy shop slows only itself (CH-1, CH-3); every deploy, migration, dashboard and alert multiplies 1,000 times; opening a shop means standing up a copy, i.e. a deploy, against CH-2.

Shared deployment (lines 27-30): a shop becomes data in the system; opening a shop is adding data (CH-2), config is data (CH-4); deploy and migration run once for all shops; isolation (CH-1, CH-3) must be done inside the system.

Splitting Ordering and Catalog (lines 31-33) answers none of the requirements because the shop is still data inside each service; the same team still changes both together, so splitting risks a distributed monolith.

Decision (lines 37-40): one shared deployment in the stage-3 shape, the only option meeting CH-2 and CH-4 without multiplying operating cost by the number of shops; how each shop's data is stored is left to a later ADR.

Consequences (lines 44-50): each request, row, message must know its shop; limits orders, catalog-reads in Program.cs do not know shops, so cannot stop one busy shop slowing others; CH-3 needs them reviewed; a bug or broken deploy reaches all shops, release must allow for it; no service added.

Reopen conditions (lines 52-57): a shop whose contract demands its own copy gets a separate copy of the same system while other shops are served as before; teams growing until they wait on each other for one module triggers a review of module (maybe service) boundaries along team lines.

At stage-3 Đơn Hàng is one deployment: DonHang.Api holds the Ordering and Catalog modules; Notifications and Payments are separate services; Ordering and Catalog stay modules in one process under ADR 0012.

Isolation is one driver among four; when a copy per shop would make opening a shop a deploy and multiply operations, the shared deployment that enforces isolation inside is the better fit for Đơn Hàng's drivers.

Trade-offs table: copy per shop costs operations growing per shop; shared deployment moves the cost into code and data, isolation built once inside, every release risks reaching every shop; split is no better than shared, adds services to run, risks a distributed monolith.

Choices: a contract demanding a copy moves only that shop onto one; teams waiting on each other: revisit module boundaries along team lines, a service only where a team boundary calls for it; a broken deploy showing only the known risk: improve releasing, not copies; a new driver reopens the ADR.

In ADR 0012 each option names the CH requirements it meets or misses, and the further split is rejected for answering no requirement and, with one team changing both, risking a distributed monolith, not for being complex.
